newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex announces job and cost cut plan.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex announces job and cost cut plan.

text.p: Moulinex announced its long-awaited cost-cutting plan on Monday and said it involved reducing the workforce by 2,600, of whom 2,100 would be in France.
The group also said it aimed to have sales of nine billion francs in three years and an operating profit of eight or nine percent of sales.
The main lines of the cost-cutting plan, which has been in the works for a long time, had already emerged via union sources last Friday.
The relaunch of the group's commercial strategy will involve limiting marketing costs to 17 percent of sales and cutting logistics costs by 10 percent, Moulinex said in a statement.
On the purchasing side, the aim was to make savings of 15 percent by changing buying procedures and concentrating the number of suppliers to cut stocks of components and raw materials.
It also said the production system would be restructured to cut costs by 25 percent outside of purchasing by improving productivity and specialising factories.
The streamlining on the jobs front would focus on limiting overtime, cutting the use of interim and fixed contract labour and other measures including aid for voluntary departures, it said.
